opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ashley Roberts (employee ID E016) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E016.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Ashley Roberts (E016), Analyst, full-time. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E016 (Ashley Roberts) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractor with basic training: max access is read (write requires advanced training). Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Security DB identifies E016 (Ashley Roberts) as a contractor with basic security training (correcting the HR note's full-time classification). Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read access; write access to Payroll was requested but exceeds the maximum. Requested level is above the max, so grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Ashley Roberts (E016), requests write access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- HR agent: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Security agent: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read.

There's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Security agent's note says "Security DB shows E016 is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted."

Who to trust? The Security agent references the Security DB, which presumably is authoritative for employment type/security training. The HR note seems to have made an error. The security agent's note is on the same ticket, correcting the earlier note. I should probably defer to the security DB as more authoritative for contractor status.

Access policy:
- contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.
- This contractor has basic security training, so max is read.
- Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

So final decision: read.

Let me submit read.
